fin.title: Radford University - Financial Requirements for international students (McGlothlin Center)

test_policy.notes: Radford is test-optional: SAT, ACT and CLT scores are not required and submitting them will not hurt a decision. Direct admission asks for a 3.0 cumulative GPA and three college-preparatory math courses; successful applicants typically have at least a 2.6 GPA. The CDS (C8) separately ticks SAT/ACT as 'not considered'.

requirements.notes: No application fee for freshmen. Apply with Radford's own application or the Common App. High school transcript required (unofficial copy accepted for review, official before enrollment); letters of recommendation are not mentioned. International applicants also submit proof of English proficiency, official transcripts in English, a passport copy, a financial statement and an Affidavit of Support if others are supporting them, and applicants from Ghana, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, The Gambia and Liberia need an official WAEC scratch card. An $800 non-refundable enrollment deposit is due after admission. Music and dance majors must audition.

deadlines.label: Early Action (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: The page prints Nov. 1 without a year; taken as fall 2027 entry. Fall decisions begin Nov. 15 and then roll out, typically 2-3 weeks after an application is complete.

deadlines.label: Regular deadline (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: The page prints Feb. 1 without a year; taken as fall 2027 entry. Rolling review continues through July 31 'as space is available'.

deadlines.label: International undergraduate fall deadline
deadlines.notes: The international requirements page lists Fall: July 1 and Spring: December 1 for undergraduates (no year printed; taken as fall 2027). The domestic freshman page gives a Feb. 1 regular date, so apply well before July 1 to leave time for the I-20 and visa.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exempt: transfer from a U.S. institution, or prior attendance at an institution in a listed waiver country (including Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Ireland, New Zealand, Jamaica and Kenya; full list on the page). Alternatives to the tests listed: SAT with a minimum 480 in Reading/Writing, TIE B2, HKDSE 4, IGCSE/GCSE/GCE grade C in English, Oxford Online Placement Test 60, NCUK EAP grade C, TOEIC 620, EIKEN Pre-1. Scores must be within the last two calendar years. No conditional admission or ESL pathway is mentioned on the page.

english.notes: Undergraduate minimum. A 1-6 band-scale minimum is not published.
Minimum 6.0 overall with at least 5.5 in Reading.

aid.notes: International freshmen and transfers are automatically considered for a merit scholarship of $6,000 to $10,000 based on the academic record in the application; no separate aid application. Radford University Foundation scholarships have applications open Nov. 1 to Feb. 5. International students are not eligible for federal aid. The international pages describe only merit awards, while the CDS (H6) ticks both need-based and non-need-based institutional aid as available to nonresidents (55 recipients, average $11,556). Proof of funds for one full year is required; the Minimum Funding table shows tuition and fees $27,682, housing $7,332, meals $5,866 and miscellaneous $7,000, with a printed total of $45,858 that does not match the line items.

sat.note: The freshman application page prints no SAT code; look up Radford University in the College Board code search.

act.note: The freshman application page prints no ACT code; look it up at act.org.

toefl.note: No TOEFL institution code is printed on the pages reviewed; confirm with admissions before sending.
